recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. The current specification should remain Reference-based; any future wording concern about Provenance.entity.what.identifier should be raised as a new targeted Provenance/Reference clarification rather than as a delayed FHIR-13570 application.
issue_request: FHIR-13570 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Security change request for STU3 asking to clarify Provenance.entity.whatUri and whatIdentifier usage, change Provenance.agent URI choices to Identifier choices, remove Provenance.entity.whatUri as redundant with whatIdentifier, and describe when Reference versus Identifier should be used.
initial_application: FHIR-13694 clarified Reference.identifier in commit ae45563ea5abedd261338cf4ff404a07a722d4ed. FHIR-13570 was then applied in commit f72fd6237875c6ba9d2a21e235881c7fed559700, changing Provenance.agent.who/onBehalfOf from uri|Reference to Identifier|Reference and Provenance.entity.what[x] from uri|Reference(Any)|Identifier to Identifier|Reference(Any).
additional_context: Later FHIR-15659 was Published/Persuasive and implemented by commit 6c0a0563b3ac6a188b713f2f1a04ff26229100cf, simplifying the same Provenance elements to Reference after logical references were introduced. The combined branch already contains a FHIR-15659 reconciliation commit. FHIR-49893 later corrected the current Provenance.entity.what comment to refer to what.identifier, and the parallel AuditEvent issue FHIR-13571 was resolved no-change based on FHIR-13694.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Provenance is active in source/fhir.ini, current source/provenance/structuredefinition-Provenance.xml defines Provenance.agent.who, Provenance.agent.onBehalfOf, and Provenance.entity.what as Reference elements, and source/datatypes/reference.xml carries the logical-reference guidance. Reintroducing URI or separate Identifier choices would reverse later final decisions.

related_jiras.note: Clarified Reference.identifier semantics and was explicitly cited by the seed and by the parallel AuditEvent no-change issue.
Removed redundant Provenance Identifier|Reference choices after logical references were introduced; already represented on the combined branch.
Corrected the current Provenance.entity.what comment to use what.identifier, confirming the current Reference.identifier model.
Parallel AuditEvent request was resolved no-change based on FHIR-13694.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification request to clarify Provenance.entity.whatUri and whatIdentifier usage and align Provenance agent/entity choices with Reference.identifier semantics.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the seed request and the STU3 decision that originally needed application.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive issue clarifying that Reference.identifier points to a structure that could potentially be expressed as a FHIR resource even when no actual FHIR instance exists.
evidence_items.learned: This is the supporting decision that FHIR-13570 and the parallel AuditEvent issue depended on.

evidence_items.summary: Provenance is an active current-build resource, and Provenance.agent.who, Provenance.agent.onBehalfOf, and Provenance.entity.what are current Reference elements without URI/Identifier choice names.
evidence_items.learned: The active current source already reflects the later Reference-based Provenance model.

evidence_items.summary: Reference.identifier carries the logical-reference definition and notes that the referenced concept need not exist as an actual FHIR instance but must fit the allowed reference type constraints.
evidence_items.learned: The general datatype now contains the clarification needed for Provenance identifier usage.

evidence_items.summary: The initial commit applied FHIR-13570 by replacing URI choices with Identifier|Reference choices; the later FHIR-15659 commit simplified the same Provenance elements to Reference.
evidence_items.learned: The current structure is explained by source history and later final decisions, so no new source edit is needed for the seed.
